delivery: evals/withskill_protocol.md wrapper, identical to reps 1-2. Serialized implementation arm.

implementation.concept: The page is a Meridian composition; scroll is the playhead over a 48-second 24fps timecode. Five acts: Overture (cloud resolves into a timeline ruler) -> Keyframes (the field BECOMES the visitor's easing curve inside an SVG editor) -> Springs (spring lattice, pluck propagates a damped wave) -> Export (particles type themselves into the real code block) -> Release (globe of meridians, draggable with inertia) + end slate showing the visitor's own curve and spring.
implementation.signature_system: One GPU point field (56,000 desktop / 16,000 mobile, a single drawArrays(POINTS)) whose formations are computed procedurally in the vertex shader from a 4-float seed and gl_VertexID. Each formation is expressed in a local square and mapped onto the DOM RECT OF THE ACT'S INSTRUMENT - 'the field literally forms on the elements in the document and travels with them as you scroll.' Morphs use per-particle staggered keyframes eased by the visitor's own cubic-bezier (same Newton solve in GLSL and JS); particles in flight glow amber ('motion has heat').
implementation.renderer: Raw WebGL2, ZERO new runtime dependencies. Two layers with separate concerns: 'SVG owns exact instrument geometry and hit targets; WebGL owns the mass.' Rejected three.js (~150 KB gz for a scene graph a one-draw-call system doesn't need) and Paper Shaders ('a second full-canvas substrate competing for the same render concern').
implementation.fit_gate: Delegated to a subagent: React Bits, Paper Shaders, SmoothUI, Fancy Components, npm versions. Nothing does DOM-anchored formation morphing (custom); spring lattice and scroll-driven playhead have reference material only (custom); bezier editors exist but only the drag maths was worth adapting; the two true drop-ins (scroll text reveals, magnet button) were DECLINED AS OFF-THESIS.
implementation.concept_family: Scroll-as-playhead again - 6 of 6 across the S1 cell (baseline reps 1-3, with-skill reps 1-3). Dark editor-frame look, so visually closer to rep1 and the baselines than to rep2's light paper world.
